series: Climate Fiscal Policy Briefs · Section 2: Other Tax and Fiscal Policy · October 2026
title: Tax Rent, Not Effort

slides.title: Tax Rent, Not Effort
slides.subtitle: Other tax and fiscal policy: section 2 in ten slides
slides.message: Free movement caps the rate on income that can move, not on rent that cannot. Tax land above a household allowance, and tax large firms' rent where it cannot leave: at origin where it is tied to the place, at destination where it follows the customer.
slides.author: Stephen J. Stretton · writing in a personal capacity

slides.text: Taxing a base that can leave invites it to leave. Rent that cannot leave can be taxed at high rates.
slides.source: OECD (2018); Tørsløv, Wier and Zucman (2023); Beer, de Mooij and Liu (2020).

slides.title: Rent can be taxed at high rates if the tax reaches it where it cannot leave

points.lead: Rent is income above what keeps an asset or a firm in use.
points.text: Taxing it changes nothing anyone does.

points.lead: Some rent is tied to a place:
points.text: land, natural resources, a large local market. Tax it at origin.

points.lead: Some rent can be booked anywhere:
points.text: patents, brands, platforms. Tax it where the customer is.
Norway taxes petroleum profit at a marginal 78% on a base that exempts the normal return.

slides.source: Mirrlees et al. (2011); Norwegian petroleum tax system (2025).

slides.title: Tax land above a household allowance, so large holdings pay and ordinary homes do not

points.lead: About 2.5% a year on site value
points.text: above an allowance close to the site value of an ordinary home.
the tax lowers land prices once and changes no use of land.
Pennsylvania cities that taxed land more than buildings saw more building.
regular revaluation, a phased rate, deferral for owners rich in land but poor in cash.

slides.title: Presume that large firms earn rent, and tax only the profit above a normal return

points.text: deduct a normal return on equity; tax the rest at 50% for large groups.
at any rate, so investment is not discouraged.

points.lead: A high rate at origin alone drives profit abroad,
points.text: so two further layers follow the customer.

slides.title: Two destination layers follow the customer, capped so low-margin firms are spared

points.text: 22% of local sales less local costs; Layer One credited.
4% of local sales, less credits of 8% of local assets and 25% of local payroll.
the destination layers stop at half the group's global rent margin times its local sales.

slides.source: Paper 2.1, Section on the corporate layers.
